text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The executive deputy chairman of South Africa's New Africa Investment Limited, Cyril Ramaphosa, said at the closure of a Southern Africa trade and investment summit in Harare on Thursday his country should not use its economic might to dominate its neighbours to the north but should adopt policies that facilitate intra-regional trade.
- Malaysian investors have been given logging concessions in close to a third of Zimbabwe's indigenous timber woosdlots in the Matebeleland and Mashonaland provinces.

- Following Zimbabwe's successful investment mission to Australia last year, which realised over Z$14 million in export orders, there are hopes for higher volumes during this year's mission in November.

- Politicians and business people committed themselves at the end of a two-day Southern Africa trade and investment conference on Thursday to co-operating and exploiting the peace currently prevailing in the region to boost economic wealth.

- State-owned Air Zimbabwe's aircraft technicians have gone on a "go-slow" over what they say are low salaries and unattractive general working conditions, leaving four of the airline's aircraft grounded.
